headlines.title: 5 revealing analyst questions from United Parcel Service’s Q3 earnings call
headlines.summary: UPS delivered a calendar Q3 that was well received by the market, with revenue and adjusted earnings per share both surpassing Wall Street expectations. Management attributed the performance to growth in premium segments, particularly within U.S. domestic operations and international trade lanes. CEO Carol Tomé highlighted that strategic investments in automation, customer mix improvements, and higher value services drove a positive spread between revenue per piece and cost per piece.

headlines.title: UPS vs. FedEx: Which Stock Is the Better Buy After Strong Q3 Results?
headlines.summary: UPS and FedEx stocks have rallied following upbeat Q3 results, but which shipping giant offers investors the better combination of growth, value, and dividend income?

headlines.title: 70% of UPS Packages Will Be Handled by Machines This Holiday Season
headlines.summary: UPS is betting that robots and radio tags can protect its dividend while it deliberately ships fewer boxes, but the math only works if one critical margin target holds during the busiest weeks of the year.

headlines.title: United Parcel Service (UPS) Attracts Ariel Global Fund on Margin Recovery and Efficiency Potential
headlines.summary: Ariel Investments, an investment management company, released its “Ariel Global Fund” Q3 2026 investor letter. The Fund declined in the third quarter of 2026 as renewed geopolitical tensions, higher oil prices, and elevated interest rates contributed to uneven performance across global markets. The Fund’s Investor Class returned -1.

headlines.title: 4 Reliable Dividend Stocks, Led by UPS, to Build Lifetime Passive Income
headlines.summary: Wall Street spent years dismissing UPS as a broken dividend story, but a fresh earnings beat changed the conversation. These four NYSE stocks now combine rising cash flow with long payout histories, and the weakest coverage ratio among them may surprise you.

description: United Parcel Service, Inc., a package delivery and logistics provider, offers transportation and delivery services. It operates through two segments, U.S. Domestic Package and International Package. The U.S. Domestic Package segment offers time-definite delivery services for express letters, documents, packages and palletized freight through air and ground services. The International Package segment provides small package operations in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, Canada and Latin America, and Asia. The company offers a range of guaranteed day- and time-definite international transportation services; day-definite services; cross-border ground package delivery; contract-only, e-commerce solutions for non-urgent, and cross-border shipments; and international service for urgent and palletized shipments. It also provides international air and ocean freight forwarding, contract logistics, customs brokerage and insurance, mail services, healthcare logistics, distribution, and post-sales services. United Parcel Service, Inc. was founded in 1907 and is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia.
